title: WastedAsphalt
tagline: Scores how empty every parking lot in a county is, using satellite images
summary: I wanted to know how much of a city is paved over for parking that nobody is using. WastedAsphalt takes every parking lot in a New York county from OpenStreetMap, grabs a satellite image of each one, and scores how much of it looks empty. Monroe County came out to 3,726 lots with a 26% average score.

overview.what: A tool that takes every parking lot in a New York county from OpenStreetMap, grabs a satellite image of each one, and scores how empty it looks.
overview.why: I wanted to know how much of a city is paved over for parking that nobody is using, and all the data to answer that is public.
overview.did: I built a FastAPI and React app that runs a whole county as a job you can pause and resume, scores each lot with OpenCV, and exports the results for ArcGIS.
overview.result: Monroe County came out to 3,726 lots with a 26% average score. The score is a simple color trick, not a car detector, so painted lines and shadows count too.

sections.heading: The idea
body: Everything you need to answer that question is public. The Census has county boundaries, OpenStreetMap already has parking lots drawn as shapes, and satellite images are one request away. WastedAsphalt connects those three and puts a number on every lot. For Monroe County it analyzed 3,697 lots (29 were skipped) in about eleven minutes.

media.caption: Picking a county.

sections.heading: Every lot, colored
body: When a county finishes, every lot shows up on the map colored by its score, from green to red. Downtown Rochester is where it gets interesting. The results export straight into ArcGIS, so they can be compared with other city data.

media.alt: Satellite map zoomed to downtown Rochester with parking lot polygons colored green, yellow, orange, and red according to their utilization score
media.caption: Downtown Rochester, one colored shape per lot.

media.alt: Completed Monroe County analysis with thousands of parking lots colored on the map and job totals in the side panels
media.caption: The whole county, finished.

sections.heading: How a lot gets scored
body: For each lot, the program finds the usual color of its asphalt and then measures how much of the lot is a different color. That's the score. The catch is that it isn't really counting cars. Painted lines, shadows and patches count too, so the lot below scored 0.91 even though it's maybe a third full. It's a simple color trick, not a trained car detector.

media.alt: Raw satellite image and analysis overlay of the same parking lot, with a teal boundary and detected anomalies highlighted over the paved surface
media.caption: The satellite image, and what the program counted. The painted stripes push the score up.

media.alt: Four Monroe County parking-lot satellite images paired with overlays marking lot boundaries in teal and detected anomalies in red
media.caption: A few more lots and their overlays.

sections.heading: Running a whole county
body: A county is thousands of image downloads, so the job can be paused and resumed, and it picks up where it left off even if the program crashes. Images are saved too, so running a county again doesn't download them twice.

notes: PROVENANCE: The expanded version was documented by running the project on 2026-09-13 on Michael's Windows machine. The existing README-derived screenshots and descriptions already on main were retained where they added useful views. The backend and frontend were run locally, the live API was inspected, and the repository's nine tests passed. FIGURES: The live API returned 62 counties, 3,726 Monroe County lots, 3,697 analyzed lots, a mean score of 0.2569, and a completed 3,698-task job with zero failures in about eleven minutes. LIMITATION: A reviewed 0.91 example showed that dense painted striping can be counted as anomaly area, so visible copy explicitly describes the result as non-asphalt occupancy rather than a trained vehicle count. MEDIA: The cover and Rochester views are real screenshots of the running app. The before-and-after image combines the raw chip and overlay written by the project. Existing county-picker, completed-run, analysis-example, and export screenshots from the repository documentation were also retained. UNVERIFIED: A fresh county run, pause and resume behavior, and the export buttons were not exercised during this portfolio pass. LINK: The public repository URL returned successfully on 2026-09-13. DATE: 2026-04 comes from the repository's first commit. None of the project's cached satellite dataset or local database is included in the portfolio.
